info_tile.heading: What is MVPF?
info_tile.description: The Marginal Value of Public Funds (MVPF) is a metric that measures the social welfare benefit of a policy per dollar of government spending. It represents how much value beneficiaries receive relative to what the policy costs.
info_tile.formula:
Most MVPF work looks at policies where the person subject to the policy is also the main beneficiary, such as cash transfers. Detention is different. Jail is imposed on detainees but is justified as benefiting the general public. That is why this tool tracks both Detainee effects and broader Society effects when calculating the MVPF of detention.

Most studies on detention focus on marginal changes, like one extra day in jail or one additional person detained. This tool instead looks at the overall or infra-marginal picture for a facility, using Cook County Jail as the baseline case. It uses the full annual costs of operating the jail and the full set of impacts on people who are detained to summarize those tradeoffs in an MVPF-style framework.

detainee_values.title: Detainee Values
detainee_values.description: Detainee Values capture the total harm detention imposes on people who are jailed. We measure this using a willingness-to-pay lens, estimating how much a person would trade to avoid being detained. This reflects short-term harms, disruptions to work and family life, and long-term effects on health, income, and stability.

harm_valuation.button_text: Willingness to Pay derived from Relative Harm Valuation
harm_valuation.explanation: The baseline detainee component, which measures harm by comparing each day in custody to crime-victimization cost benchmarks such as robbery or aggravated assault. This produces a larger per-day harm value than detainee self-reported WTP (~$4,000/day), and scales with whatever length of stay (non-linearly), population, or charge mix the user chooses. Because it reflects broader social harm rather than ability-to-pay limits, it is used as the default. Source: crime-harm equivalence estimates from Stevenson & Mayson (2022).

wtp_freedom.explanation: An alternative detainee valuation based on stated willingness-to-pay (WTP) per day to avoid jail, drawn from surveys of people facing detention. Valued at $11/day in 2018 dollars. This approach reflects detainees' own monetary tradeoffs and can be scaled using any assumed length of stay or detainee population. It typically produces much smaller harm estimates than the baseline Relative Harm Valuation, which makes the overall MVPF less negative and is therefore a more conservative choice. Source: detainee WTP evidence summarized in Stevenson & Mayson (2022).

society_values.title: Society Values
society_values.description: Society Values measure how detention affects external factors like public safety, victimization risk, and community wellbeing. These values summarize the effects felt by people outside the jail and convert those effects into a common dollar scale for comparison.

crime_prevention.explanation: This component captures any crime-prevention benefit from incapacitation during detention. In the baseline model, this is set to zero in line with empirical evidence suggesting minimal net crime reduction from pretrial detention. Users can adjust this assumption in alternative scenarios.

court_appearance.explanation: Included as a baseline society component because court appearance is a central justification for pretrial detention. This component places a dollar value on avoiding failures to appear (FTA) by combining administrative costs of warrant issuance and possible rearrest with an assumed FTA probability. Source: Fishbane, Ouss & Shah (2020) and Cook County court data.

community_spillovers.explanation: This component captures broader community effects of detention, including impacts on families, neighborhoods, and local economies. Effects include lost wages, disrupted caregiving, and reduced community stability. These spillovers extend the costs of detention beyond the individual detainee.

government_cost.title: Government Cost
government_cost.description: Government Cost reflects all public spending required to run the detention system. This includes daily operations, staffing, healthcare, facilities, court processing, and administrative overhead. It represents the fiscal cost taxpayers bear to support the current level of detention.

operational.explanation: The baseline government cost component, representing the full operating budgets for the Cook County Department of Corrections and Cermak Health Services. These expenses include staffing, food, medical care, housing, and other daily operations, and they can be allocated over any assumed detainee count or length of stay. Since these costs reflect actual fiscal outlays, they form the default denominator of the MVPF. Source: Cook County FY2018 Appropriation Budget.

crime_increase.button_text: Costs associated with Crime Effect: Increase
crime_increase.explanation: Government costs that arise if detention leads to increased crime post-release (criminogenic effect). This includes additional law enforcement, court processing, victim services, and potential future incarceration costs. Evidence suggests detention can increase recidivism for some populations.

crime_decrease.button_text: Costs associated with Crime Effect: Decrease
crime_decrease.explanation: Government savings that occur if detention prevents crimes through incapacitation or deterrence. This includes avoided law enforcement costs, reduced court processing, and lower victim compensation. The magnitude depends on assumptions about detention's crime-prevention effectiveness.
